work_order.understanding:
Issue #78 collects 10 review findings and 2 QA findings from PR #62 (for #61). I re-checked all twelve against HEAD (632153e) by mutation rather than by reading, and confirmed the proposer's split: four are real code defects, two QA findings no longer reproduce, and six are about the PR record, a reserved path, or comment hygiene rather than about code.

STILL BROKEN, each reproduced by me at HEAD:

1. Review finding 1 — the table-scroll region guard asks for its three attributes with \b (test/web/pages.test.js:1875, :1879, :1880). '-' is a non-word character, so \baria-label= also matches the tail of data-aria-label=. Mutating src/web/pages.js:106 to emit data-tabindex/data-role/data-aria-label leaves the suite at 71 pass / 1 fail, byte-identical to baseline. The keyboard-reachability contract cannot fail.

2. Review finding 3 — the same \b defect in the h1 styling-class guard (pages.test.js:1626). Mutating src/web/pages.js:60 to <h1 data-class="page-title"> leaves the suite unchanged.

2b. (Neither the proposal nor the issue names this, but it is the same family and I verified it.) H1_HOOK at pages.test.js:23 is /<h1[^>]*\bdata-testid="page-title"[^>]*>[^<]*<\/h1>/. I ran it: against <h1 class="page-title" foo-data-testid="page-title"> it returns TRUE — the hyphen before 'data-testid' is a word boundary. The 25-shell h1 assertion is pinned through H1_HOOK, so a page whose only h1 hook is a forged attribute passes the whole file green. Contrast mainOf at :35, which genuinely uses \s and returns '' for <main data-id="main">. The family's closure claim is false unless this site is included.

3. Review finding 2 — the load-time failure announcement. src/web/client.js:56 writes to #live-region from a defer script (pages.js:87), i.e. before the load event, the window in which polite live-region updates are commonly not announced at all. This is the design question the review says neither reviewer settled, and it is the mechanism the failure announcement rests on.

4. Review finding 4 — errorShellHarness can only observe focus() on the one element it stubs. Inserting `document.querySelector('#main').focus()` into client.js leaves the suite at 71/1. The test's own comment claims more than the recorder delivers.

5. Review finding 5 — the page-state sentence is destroyed. #live-region is a single textContent node (pages.js:79) and client.js writes to it twice on load (:24 and :56), so the second write wins. On the five ?state=error shells the panel is a PREVIEW, so a screen-reader user is told a named scenario failed for real; on ?meta_error=quota the user also loses the page's identity.

5b. (Also mine, and the most consequential thing here.) The proposal's fix for 3 and 5 — compose one message and write it after load — is itself defective as described, and I am rewriting it rather than applying it. loadMessage() as specified reads region.textContent at load time as its head. But the retry, drawer and approval handlers are all attached when the deferred script runs, which is BEFORE load, so a user-initiated announcement can land in the region first. The deferred write then either overwrites it or absorbs it as if it were the server-rendered decision receipt. The proposal's risk entry dismisses this by asserting those announcements are 'user-initiated and long past load', which is false for exactly the case the deferral exists to serve: a page whose load is stalled. See root_cause and AC-4.

ALREADY FIXED at HEAD — these two QA findings do not reproduce and I am dropping them rather than implementing something that was never wrong:

- QA finding 1 (Retry autofocuses on load, pre-empting the first Tab): client.js has no load-time focus() at all. `grep -n 'focus()' src/web/client.js` returns exactly two sites, :96 (closeDrawer restoring focus to the invoking row) and :154 (the drawer opening on an explicit click). #61's own change removed the autofocus; this finding describes origin/main, not HEAD.
- QA finding 2 (\bid="main" matching data-id="main"): mainOf at pages.test.js:35 already uses \sid="main" and already returns '' for the data-id spelling (I ran it), the four data-* negatives already sit at pages.test.js:313-326, and src/web/pages.js:80 emits <main id="main" tabindex="-1">. No \bid= site survives in test/.

NOT ACTIONABLE FROM A TICKET — three review findings are about the PR record or a reserved path. Review finding 6 (two lines of .sdlc/memory/qa/selectors.md are now false) names a path this ticket may not write; I record both lines in risks for the Librarian. Review findings 7 and 8 are statements about PR #62's body and work order, which are historical. Review finding 9 (the \s rationale written out twice, ~180 lines apart) is a comment-duplication cleanup and finding 10 (a test asserting stylesheet byte order) explicitly asks for no change.

The work that remains is five defects with one shape: a guard that cannot fail, a signal written twice and therefore lost, a deferral that trades one lost signal for another, and a harness that models a hand-picked subset of the browser and so cannot see a new API being used.
work_order.root_cause:
Three distinct causes, and the third is the one that made the first two hard to fix.

(a) Mutation-invisible guards. The \b matcher asserts a word boundary, not whitespace, so any hyphenated attribute ending in the name satisfies it. The \b -> \s hardening in PR #62 was applied to the two guards its work order named and stopped; four more sites in the same file kept the idiom, each mutation-invisible to exactly the data-* spelling that would break the thing it guards. The h1 styling-class site, the table-scroll site and H1_HOOK are the same defect in the same family.

(b) A signal written twice. client.js made two separate announce() calls on load — the page-state sentence at :24 and the failure sentence at :56. #live-region is one textContent node, so the second write silently replaced the first. The timing defect (finding 2) and the signal-loss defect (finding 5) are one bug seen from two sides.

(c) A deferral that trades one lost signal for another. Writing once after load fixes (b), but the handlers for retry, drawer and approvals are attached at script-evaluation time — before load — so a user-initiated announcement can arrive first. A deferred write that reads the region at load time then absorbs that announcement as if it were the server-rendered decision receipt, or overwrites it. The fix is not 'write after load' but 'write after load, and never over a signal that arrived first': capture the server-rendered receipt once at evaluation time into a local, and have announceOnLoad() skip the write entirely if announce() has been called since the script loaded. The one case that legitimately needs the region read is the decision-receipt hand-off, and reading it once at evaluation is sufficient.

(d) The harness limitation (finding 4) is a fourth cause, and the critique was right that the proposal named it too narrowly. It is not that the harness can only see one element's focus(); it is that both harnesses model a hand-picked subset of the browser and are not kept in step with what client.js touches. Any new use of a window or document API in client.js throws a TypeError in every test that loads it, silently — which is exactly what happens to draftHarness (pages.test.js:1058), the second harness, the moment client.js reads a load event. The harnesses are the same mutation-invisible family as (a): they cannot see a change, and the suite being green says nothing.
work_order.approach:
Three files, all confined to src/web/client.js and test/web/pages.test.js.

1. Close the \b family at all four remaining sites, not the two the proposal named. Extract a `scrollRegionName(tag)` helper from the inline assertions at pages.test.js:1875-1880 (asking for \saria-label=, \stabindex="0", \srole="region", returning the label or null), a `h1Class(tag)` helper for the guard at :1626, and change H1_HOOK at :23 to ask for \sdata-testid= so it cannot be satisfied by the tail of a forged attribute. Each is then asked directly of hand-written markup, so the data-* negatives are assertions against the real matcher rather than comments claiming one exists. This mirrors the shape PR #62 established for skipLinkFocusesMain at pages.test.js:225-338 — positives, order-tolerance, then one negative per failure mode.

2. Compose the load message and write it once, after load, without ever clobbering. At script-evaluation time, capture the server-rendered region text into a local (`serverAnnouncement`) — that is the decision-receipt hand-off and it must survive. Replace the two announce() calls with `loadMessage()`, which returns `serverAnnouncement` when it is non-empty, else the page-state sentence, and appends the failure sentence when a .panel-error is present (reading the panel's own <h2> defensively, preserving the 'This page failed to load' fallback). The two are joined with a single space, so the page-state sentence keeps its shipped copy verbatim and gains no terminator it did not have. `announceOnLoad()` writes it from a window 'load' listener, or synchronously if document.readyState is already 'complete', and returns without writing if `announce()` has already been called since the script loaded — that is what keeps a retry or drawer announcement made on a still-loading page from being absorbed or overwritten. The registration is guarded so a second entry cannot double-fire. Both the region-null case (announce() already no-ops) and the headingless-panel fallback degrade exactly as they do today.

3. Fix the harness as a class, not as one selector. Extract a shared `clientDom()` stub factory that supplies the window/document surface client.js actually touches — getElementById, querySelector, querySelectorAll, addEventListener, readyState, window.addEventListener, window.localStorage, window.location — and have both draftHarness (pages.test.js:1039-1065) and errorShellHarness (:1080-1120) build on it. errorShellHarness additionally gains focus-recording stubs for #main and a.skip-link that querySelector answers for, plus a `readyState` and a `finishLoading()` that flips readyState to 'complete' and fires the registered load handlers. This is the difference between fixing the test that broke and fixing the reason a second harness was invisible: with one factory, the next window API added to client.js has one place to be stubbed.

4. Assert the ordering, the negatives, and the two paths the proposal left uncovered. The announcement test asserts the region is EMPTY before finishLoading() and populated after, and that the message begins with the page-state sentence, so a preview shell is distinguishable from a real failure. A new test covers the path the proposal admits no test covers: a server-rendered decision receipt present together with an error panel — the receipt must be the head of the composed message, not overwritten. A new test covers the clobber: an announcement made before finishLoading() survives it, and finishLoading() adds nothing. A new test covers the receipt surviving a plain load with no panel. Three negative tests cover the data-* spellings of the region attributes, data-class on the h1, and a forged data-testid against H1_HOOK; a fourth covers a focus steal aimed at #main and at a.skip-link.

I built and mutation-verified all of this in a scratch copy before writing it here. With the fix in place, each mutation the original suite missed (data-* table-scroll, data-class h1, forged data-testid, focus steal on #main or .skip-link) turns it red, as do the regressions: reverting the write to pre-load timing, reverting to the two-write form, and making the deferred write clobber a pre-load announcement. Full suite: 473 tests, 472 pass, 1 fail — the one failure being the pre-existing approval-card test, which this order carries as a one-line fix (see risks).

risks: The load-time announcement now waits for the window load event. If a resource the page is waiting on stalls, the announcement is delayed with it. That is the trade for a polite region actually being announced, and it is bounded by the AC-4 guard: a user-initiated announcement made during the stall is never overwritten, so the delay costs latency on the page-state sentence and never costs a signal.

The composed message is longer than either sentence was alone. A screen reader reading both clauses is the intent, but it is a copy change a human may want to word differently; the strings are all in one place in client.js if so. The join is a single space, so the shipped page-state sentence keeps its exact current wording and gains no terminator.

The decision receipt the server rendered into #live-region is now the HEAD of the composed message rather than something the failure sentence overwrites. That is a behaviour change on /approvals?decision=... when a panel is also present, and it is the fix — AC-5 adds the test the proposal says was missing.

The full suite is RED at HEAD, before this change: 'the approval action row can shrink, and the selectors below have something to match' (test/web/pages.test.js:1756) fails because the assertion at :1779 is /<li class="approval-card">/ and src/web/pages.js:1043 now emits <li class="approval-card" data-testid=... data-approval-card ...>. It is the same family as the rest of this ticket but from the opposite direction — an over-strict matcher that breaks when an attribute is ADDED — and it was introduced by 37f9576 (#53), not by #61. I am overriding the proposal, which put it out of scope and left the choice to the implementer: sdlc:verify is npm ci && node --test, so a branch that leaves it red cannot be verified at all, and one line in a file this change already edits is a smaller cost than a permanently red gate. It is called out here because it is a deliberate scope decision, not an oversight.

QA finding 2 (\bid="main" matching data-id) no longer reproduces — mainOf already uses \s and the four data-* negatives are already present at pages.test.js:313-326. A file-wide self-guard against \b attribute matchers reopening. I measured it: it produces 57 hits on the current file, essentially all legitimate — fixture strings like /<li class="approval-card">/ and the twenty-odd skipLinkFocusesMain('...') markup literals at pages.test.js:270-335, which is where the \b POSITIVES deliberately live. A guard that fires on its own file's test data trains the next reader to delete it. The targeted route is better and is what this order does: extract each matcher to a named helper and assert the negatives against the helper.

The full end-to-end screen-reader pass review finding 2 asks for, beyond the two shells in AC-7. A real AT pass cannot be automated in this pipeline; qa_script drives a human through both reachable shells and the outcome is recorded in the PR.

Any change to the shipped copy of the page-state sentence, the failure sentence, or the panel headings. The announcement is derived from what the page already renders, per docs/ui.md's rule that an error panel states what failed; this change moves WHEN it is written and WHAT it carries, not what it says. The two sentences are joined with a single space and the page-state sentence keeps its exact current wording, terminator included.
work_order.confidence_rationale: High on the five defects and on the harness root cause: I reproduced each by mutation at HEAD and verified each fix by re-running the same mutation against the patched suite, so the causal chain is measured rather than argued, and I re-ran the critique's central claim myself (both window stubs lack addEventListener; H1_HOOK matches a forged foo-data-testid; the page-state sentence has no trailing full stop) rather than taking it on trust. The 22-point discount is for two things. First, the one I could not settle: whether a polite live region written after the load event is actually announced in a real screen reader — the reviewer's own open question, unanswerable from this repo, and AC-7 depends on a human with a browser. Second, the composed copy has never been heard, and the AC-4 guard is reasoned from the code's own structure rather than observed in a browser under a stalled load; it is mutation-verified in the harness but the harness is not a browser. What would move this up: an AT pass answering AC-7 in the affirmative, and the suite green on the branch as AC-8 specifies. What would move it down: an AT pass answering AC-7 in the negative, which would mean the deferral is not the mechanism and the fix has to be re-derived.

alternatives_considered.approach: Apply the proposal's fix for findings 2 and 5 as written: loadMessage() reads region.textContent at load time as its head, and announceOnLoad() writes it unconditionally.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: I rejected the proposal rather than applying it here. The read-at-load-time is the defect: every user-initiated handler (retry, drawer, approvals) is attached before the load event, so on a page whose load is stalled — the exact case the deferral exists to serve — a user announcement is either overwritten or absorbed as if it were the server-rendered decision receipt. The proposal's own risk entry asserts the opposite is true ('user-initiated and long past load'), which is a claim about the code's structure that does not hold. Reading the region once at script-evaluation time into a local, and skipping the deferred write if announce() has fired since, closes it at no cost. The evidence array names the two mutations that catch this.

alternatives_considered.approach: A file-wide self-guard: a test that greps test/web/pages.test.js for any \b(id|tabindex|class|href|role|aria-label)=" and fails if one survives, so the family cannot reopen.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: I measured it: 57 hits on the current file, essentially all legitimate — fixture strings like /<li class="approval-card">/, assert.match(html, /class="skeleton /), and the twenty-odd skipLinkFocusesMain('...') markup literals at pages.test.js:270-335, which is where the \b POSITIVES deliberately live. A guard that fires on its own file's test data trains the next reader to delete it. The targeted route is better and is mutation-verified: extract each matcher to a named helper and assert the negatives against the helper, which is the shape PR #62 already established for skipLinkFocusesMain.

alternatives_considered.approach: A guard test that fails when client.js references a window or document property the shared stub does not define (the critique's option (b) for the harness root cause).
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Same failure mode as the self-guard above, and I declined it for the same reason: it greps a file for a pattern and fires on that file's own legitimate test data — client.js legitimately uses a dozen window and document members, and a static scan cannot tell a modelled member from a legitimately unmodelled one without a hand-maintained allowlist, which is the same drift the guard was meant to stop. I took the critique's option (a), one shared stub factory, which fixes the actual cause (two hand-built harnesses, one of them invisible) rather than adding a second kind of grep. The critique's diagnosis of the cause was right and I kept it; I am recording that I did not take its preferred fix.

alternatives_considered.approach: Leave the announcement timing alone and only fix the signal loss — fold the state into the failure sentence, keeping the write where it is (before load).
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It closes finding 5 and leaves finding 2 — the actual design question — untouched, and finding 2 is the one the reviewer says neither they nor the work order settled. A write during parse is the window in which polite regions are commonly not announced at all, so the composed sentence would be one a screen reader may never read. Writing once, after load, with the AC-4 guard against clobbering, closes both with one change.

alternatives_considered.approach: Restore the focus() on the failing panel's retry button as a guaranteed-announcement mechanism, and keep the live-region write as secondary.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: This is what #61 removed on purpose, and QA finding 1 exists because it broke AC-1: the skip link was never the first Tab on any error shell. Restoring it re-breaks the guarantee this repo most recently paid for, and the harness work in item 3 exists precisely so the bypass cannot be re-broken silently.

alternatives_considered.approach: Use an assertive role="alert" region for the failure instead of deferring the polite one, on the theory that assertive updates are announced during parse.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It changes the politeness contract rather than the timing, and a load-time assertive interrupt on a page the user has not yet read is worse behaviour than a slightly late polite announcement. docs/ui.md asks for state changes to be announced via aria-live, not for interrupts. The load-listener fix addresses the actual defect with no change to the region's semantics.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix only the two named \b sites and drop the announcement findings as an AT question better settled in a browser.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: That is the shape of plan that gets the same verdict rejected a second time: findings 2 and 5 are code defects with a known cause (two writes to a single textContent node, from a deferred script) and a measured fix, not open questions. The genuinely open part — whether a screen reader announces it — is isolated in AC-7 where a human can answer it, instead of being used as a reason to leave the two-write bug in place.

assumptions: That 'after the load event' is materially better than 'after DOMContentLoaded' for a polite live region. Both are outside the initial-parse window the review names, and load is the one the review's own fix suggests ('e.g. from a `load` listener or a one-frame deferral'). I did not verify this against a screen reader; it is AC-7.

That document.readyState === 'complete' is the right synchronous fallback. In a real browser the deferred script runs while readyState is 'loading' or 'interactive', so the listener is the normal path and the synchronous branch is for a late-registered script and for the harness. The listener registration is guarded against a second entry.

That reading the server-rendered region once at script-evaluation time is equivalent to reading it at load time for the decision-receipt hand-off. Nothing writes to the region between script evaluation and load except client.js's own handlers, and those are exactly what the AC-4 guard declines to overwrite — so the two reads differ only on a path we do not want.
That the twenty-five-shell render loop and the seeded fixtures are unaffected. This change edits no server-rendered markup, one client script, and matchers in one test file.

That a human with a browser is available for AC-7. Nothing in this pipeline can drive a screen reader, and .sdlc/memory/qa/environment.md records no AT capability. If no one runs it, AC-7 is unmet and AC-3's test half is the whole of what has been proven.

That fixing the red approval-card matcher here is the right scope call rather than filing it. The implementer may reasonably disagree; if they do, the alternative is a permanently red CI, which is worse. The one-line relaxation is called out separately in risks and in AC-8 so it is reviewable on its own.
unknowns: Whether a polite live region written from a load listener is announced in the real screen readers this project cares about. Nothing in the repo can answer it; it needs a human with a browser and it is AC-7.
Whether the composed message reads acceptably end to end. The two sentences were written separately and this change joins them with a space; nobody has heard the result.

Whether pairing the 'preview state' wording with a failure sentence in one message reads well. On ?state=error the panel is a preview and the body state says so, but the two halves now sit in one sentence and the interaction may read oddly.

Whether a real browser under a genuinely stalled load behaves as the AC-4 guard assumes. The harness fires the load handlers deterministically; it cannot reproduce a resource that never finishes. The guard is reasoned from the wiring (every handler attaches before load) and mutation-verified, not browser-verified.

Whether a title containing '·' inside the page name still truncates. `document.title.split('·')[0].trim()` at client.js:23 is the source of the page name, and it is pre-existing — but the announcement is now composed, so the truncation is more visible beside the failure sentence. Not this ticket's change and not measured.
work_order.debate_summary:
The critique was right about the diagnosis and right about one thing the proposal got wrong, and I have rewritten the plan rather than patching it.

What I accepted and folded in. (1) The proposal's central empirical claim is false. I re-ran it myself: both window stubs in test/web/pages.test.js lack addEventListener and readyState, so the client.js change as specified takes the file from 71 pass / 1 fail to 67 pass / 5 fail, and the two tests that pin this ticket's own behaviour are among the casualties. The proposal names only errorShellHarness; draftHarness is the second harness and appears nowhere in it. (2) The harness framing was too narrow. It is not that errorShellHarness can only see one element's focus(); it is that the harnesses model a hand-picked subset of the browser, which is why an unstubbed API breaks every test that loads client.js silently. I restated the root cause accordingly and made the fix a shared stub factory rather than a selector addition. (3) The proposal declares the \b family closed with a grep that does not reach H1_HOOK at pages.test.js:23. I ran it: H1_HOOK matches <h1 class="page-title" foo-data-testid="page-title">, and the 25-shell h1 assertion is pinned through it. Neither the issue nor the proposal names this site. It is in files[] and AC-2, and I rewrote AC-2's closure claim to say honestly what the grep covers and name H1_HOOK as the site it does not. (4) The test case and the out_of_scope list contradicted each other: the source produces 'Decision journal is showing the error preview state' with no trailing full stop and the case asserted one with it. I resolved it toward the copy constraint — single-space join, assertion without the terminator — and said so in the order. (5) The clobber hazard is the most consequential of all and neither the proposal nor the issue raises it. The proposal's fix for findings 2 and 5 is itself defective: loadMessage() reads the region at load time, but every user-initiated handler attaches before load, so a retry or drawer announcement on a still-loading page is absorbed as a decision receipt or overwritten. This is not a nitpick — it trades one lost signal for another on exactly the path the deferral was introduced to serve. I rewrote the approach around it (capture the receipt at evaluation time, skip the write if announce() has fired) and gave it its own acceptance criterion with the two mutations that catch it.

What I rejected. The critique's option (b) for the harness root cause — a guard test that fails when client.js references a window/document property the stub lacks. The diagnosis behind it is right and I kept the diagnosis; the fix is the same shape as the file-wide \b self-guard the proposal already built and measured at 57 legitimate hits. A static scan cannot tell a modelled member from a legitimately unmodelled one without an allowlist, which is the drift the guard exists to prevent. I took option (a), one shared factory. The critique's minor finding on AC-3/AC-5 verify modes is right in substance and I acted on it by splitting the criterion: AC-3 is now verify:test and names the gate's actual assertion, AC-7 carries the browser half. Its minor finding on QA finding 1 asks for nothing and I agree — I recorded that I checked whether the no-focus guarantee is load-bearing and nothing depends on it.

Where I overrode the proposal. It put the red approval-card test out of scope and left the choice to the implementer, on the reasoning that it belongs to #53. sdlc:verify is npm ci && node --test, so a branch that leaves it red cannot be verified at all; the critique pressed this and I agree with the pressure. It is one line in a file this change already edits, it is the same defect family, and I verified the relaxation matches the shipped markup while rejecting the data-* forgery. It is in files[], in AC-8, and separately in risks so it is reviewable on its own. A reviewer who thinks it belongs in its own ticket can split it out; what they cannot do is ship the branch red.

Where the council did not converge and I am not pretending it did. The proposal was confident that the announcement fix was verified by mutation; the critique showed the fix itself was unverified and broken. I have now mutation-verified the corrected version, but only in a harness — a real browser under a genuinely stalled load is not something this pipeline can produce, and AC-7 is the only place that gap is addressed, by a human. That is the main reason confidence is 78 and not higher.
residual_risks: The screen-reader question itself (AC-7). QA should go here first. Nothing in the suite distinguishes 'written to the region' from 'announced', so a green CI says nothing about whether this ticket's central behaviour change helps a screen-reader user at all.

The AC-4 clobber guard under a genuinely stalled load, in a real browser. The harness fires load deterministically; it cannot reproduce a resource that never completes. If a reviewer wants this exercised for real, it needs a page served with a deliberately slow resource.

The composed message copy. It has never been read aloud. QA should read it on both shells and report whether 'Decision journal is showing the error preview state Replay evaluation failed for scenario replay-tracking-outage. Use Retry to try again.' is acceptable, particularly on the preview shells where nothing has actually failed.

Whether the deferral delays the announcement noticeably on a slow connection — the risk is latency on the page-state sentence, never a lost signal, but a user who has already read the page may hear the state sentence late.

The two false lines in .sdlc/memory/qa/selectors.md (line 8 and line 21) that this ticket cannot fix. QA reads that file; both lines are wrong against this branch and one of them becomes wrong in a new way here.

A page title containing '·' inside the page name truncates the announcement's page name. Pre-existing at client.js:23, not caused by this change, and not measured — but more visible now that the announcement is composed with the failure sentence.
